official_questions.stem: Syadvada school of philosophy was propounded by

official_questions.stem: Who of the following is considered as the founder of the Satavahana rule ?

statements.t: The king who bore the title Kavivatsala was Gautamiputra Satakarni.

official_questions.stem: According to the Nasik inscription of Rishabhadatta, the rate of interest during the Satavahana period was

official_questions.rule: Nasik guild deposits: 2,000 @ 12%, 1,000 @ 9%.

official_questions.stem: The Myakadoni inscription refers to the word "Gulmika" to mean
official_questions.core_fact: The Myakadoni inscription of Pulumavi (Bellary) mentions a 'gumika/gulmika' of a village; the key reads it as village head; app notes describe the gaulmika as head of a gulma (village cluster/military outpost).

statements.t: In the Myakadoni inscription Gulmika means village head.

official_questions.rule: Satavahana officers: Amatya, Mahamatra, Gaulmika (gulma head), Gramika (village).
official_questions.key_note: App notes describe the gaulmika as head of a gulma or military-outpost officer rather than strictly a village head; key kept.

official_questions.stem: The Jain philosopher who composed "Samayasara" was
official_questions.core_fact: Samayasara (with Pravachanasara, Panchastikayasara, Niyamasara) is by the Digambara teacher Kundakundacharya (associated with Konakondla, Anantapur).

official_questions.stem: The Jataka literature which refers to the defeat of Kharavela, the Kalinga king, at the hands of Satakarni, the Asmaka king, was
official_questions.core_fact: The Chulla-Kalinga Jataka tells of the Kalinga king's defeat by the Assaka (Asmaka) king; the APPSC line reads it as Satakarni defeating Kharavela. The Serivanija Jataka mentions Andhapura on the Telavaha.

statements.t: The Serivanija Jataka refers to the defeat of the Kalinga king by the Asmaka king.

official_questions.key_note: Third-party compilation keys Serivanija; stored key (Chulla-Kalinga) matches app notes. Identification with Kharavela/Satakarni is APPSC's reading.

official_questions.stem: During whose regnal period did Buddhism receive great patronage in the Ikshvaku kingdom ?
official_questions.core_fact: Buddhism reached its peak at Nagarjunakonda under Mathariputra Virapurushadatta, whose queens and princesses (Chamtisri etc.) built stupas and viharas.

official_questions.rule: Ikshvakus: Chantamula I (Vedic), Virapurushadatta (Buddhist peak), Ehuvala (temples), Rudrapurushadatta (last).

official_questions.stem: What was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi ?

official_questions.stem: Which of the following was the capital of Ikshvakus ?

official_questions.stem: Amaravati Stupa was built during the rule of

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is false with regards to socio-religious and economic conditions during the Satavahana rule ?

The women were looked down upon
There was a flourishing maritime trade

official_questions.core_fact: Puranas call them Andhrabhrityas; Vasishthiputra Satakarni/Pulumavi issued bilingual Prakrit-Tamil (Dravidian) coins; they patronised Brahmanism and Buddhism; their marriage alliance was with the Western Kshatrapas (Rudradaman), not the much later Kakatiyas (12th c.).

statements.fact: Their marriage alliance was with the Western Kshatrapas (Rudradaman's daughter); Kakatiyas came ~900 years later.

official_questions.rule: Satavahana alliances: Western Kshatrapas; any medieval dynasty is anachronistic.
